issues.display_title: Issue #505: Remove Auto Fit Plan on Change Area Type
issues.main_description_html:
RESULT

Merged via PR #558.

Root cause: changing a room's type (setAreaType, a store-side edit) reloads the engine model, and applyModel's default path re-frames exactly like the Fit Plan button (fit2D + resetCam).

Fix: pass the caller's existing isStoreEdit flag as loadModel's existing keepView param (one line in FloorplanEditor.tsx) — store edits (setAreaType, setAreaInfo, …) keep the user's pan/zoom + 3D camera; level switches and first loads still re-frame. Same preserve-the-view rule collab already used.

Tests: 2 new (applyModel keepView routing). Suite 801 pass, lint + tsc clean.

issues.display_title: Issue #561: Map mode: drag-to-move shifts every building instead of the selected one (PRD #536 R13/R16)
issues.main_description_html:
PRD #536 validation gap 1 of 5 (R13 / R16). Highest severity of the five.

Description

src/lib/map/useBuildingDrag.ts was never updated for per-building placement (#548). Its Options type takes no building id, and the building-scope branch still writes the project-wide mapOffsetX / mapOffsetY (useBuildingDrag.ts:86-92), which makePixelRotator (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:107-127) applies to every building.

Consequences with 2+ buildings:

  • Drag-to-move (the primary move gesture, Map mode → "Drag building") shifts the whole project, not the selected building — R13 is only satisfied by the popup's small nudge arrows.
  • Dragging one building moves the others — direct R16 violation ("moving one building must not move other buildings").

Secondary defect in the same file: the floor-scope drag inverse (useBuildingDrag.ts:74-77) ignores the building's own mapTransform rotation/scale, unlike the nudge path which composes it correctly (src/components/editor/MapTransformControl.tsx:273-288). A floor drag on a rotated or scaled building therefore travels in the wrong direction/distance.

Fix direction

Route the drag's building branch through the same targetBuildingOf + patchBuildingTransform logic MapTransformControl uses, and compose the building frame into the floor-scope inverse. Fall back to the project-wide offset only when the project has no Building records (legacy).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Dragging in building scope moves only the selected building; sibling buildings are byte-identical
  • Legacy projects (no buildings) keep writing the project-wide offset — behavior unchanged
  • Floor-scope drag on a rotated/scaled building tracks the pointer correctly
  • Unit test: drag commit isolates the target building (rotate/scale isolation asserted too, not just translation)
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #562: Delete building leaves implicit-default levels behind and re-homes them (PRD #536 R7)
issues.main_description_html:
PRD #536 validation gap 2 of 5 (R7).

Description

deleteBuilding cascades only levels explicitly stamped with the deleted building's id (src/store/mapStore/buildingsSlice.ts:72 filters l.buildingId === id). But the project's one scoping rule (src/lib/editor/levels.ts:114-125) says a level with no buildingId belongs to the implicit default building — buildings[0] — and the UI lists those levels under it.

Reproduction: an older project (levels carry no buildingId) → add Building A, then Building B → delete Building A. A's listed levels survive the delete and silently re-home into Building B. This contradicts the confirmation dialog's copy ("This also removes every level inside this building") and R7. The zero-levels safety guard (buildingsSlice.ts:76) never fires for this case either, so the refusal path can't catch it.

Fix direction

Build the cascade's membership set with levelsInBuilding(levels, buildings, id) instead of the raw buildingId === id filter, so implicit-default levels are included when buildings[0] is the target. The existing zero-levels guard then works as intended.

Related minor issue worth folding in: when the guard refuses a delete (it would leave the project with zero levels) the UI gives no feedback — the confirm just closes and nothing happens (src/components/editor/ManageBuildingsModal.tsx:101-131).

Acceptance Criteria

  • Deleting buildings[0] also removes levels that carry no buildingId
  • Deleting a non-first building is unchanged
  • The zero-levels refusal still holds, and the user sees why the delete did not happen
  • Cascade stays one undoable history snapshot
  • Unit test: implicit-default levels are cascaded
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #563: Outdoor mode leaks safety markers + pano lines and stays editable (PRD #536 R22/R25)
issues.main_description_html:
PRD #536 validation gap 3 of 5 (R22 / R25).

Description

Safety markers and pano connection lines leak into outdoor mode on every surface. src/lib/map/useFloorPlanLabels.ts draws markers (lines 184-243) and connection lines (247-261) before the if (!visibleRef.current) return gate at line 303 — deliberate so they survive the "Show labels" toggle, but it means the visible: !outdoor prop passed by the editor (Editor3DMapView.tsx:178) and the viewer (PreviewOverlay.tsx:328) only hides labels. Safety markers also stay clickable (useFloorPlanLabels.ts:432-437), and clicking one opens SelectedFeaturePanel for editing.

R25 requires outdoor mode to hide indoor labels, points, shapes, safety markers, panorama markers, and directions. R22 requires outdoor mode to be view-only.

Editor outdoor mode is not view-only either:

  • "Drag building" move mode is gated on mapMoveMode alone, never on outdoor (Editor3DMapView.tsx:197-205, useBuildingDrag.ts:41), and EditorBottomToolbar renders unconditionally (Editor3DMapView.tsx:355) — a drag while outdoor commits placement mutations to canvasData.
  • Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y undo/redo hotkeys stay live (Editor3DMapView.tsx:249-258).

Fix direction

One place for the leak: null the markers / connectionLines inputs (or gate the whole draw) when outdoor, rather than adding a second flag to each caller. Separately, make outdoor engage exit mapMoveMode and gate the drag/toolbar on !outdoor.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Outdoor mode hides safety markers and pano connection lines on editor Map mode, /preview, /v/[key], and /embed
  • Nothing indoor is clickable while outdoor (no selection panel opens)
  • Building drag cannot mutate placement while outdoor; move mode exits when outdoor engages
  • "Show labels" toggle behavior is unchanged when indoor
  • Unit test: outdoor hides indoor draw inputs
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #564: Preview/live: search, deep link and tour sync desync the selected building (PRD #536 R35)
issues.main_description_html:
PRD #536 validation gap 4 of 5 (R35).

Description

On the public surfaces (/preview, /v/[key], /embed — all PreviewOverlay.tsx) three navigation paths change the active level without re-pointing selectedBuildingId:

  • search result pick — PreviewOverlay.tsx:429-435
  • ?panoId deep link — PreviewOverlay.tsx:128
  • tourmkr sync switchLevel — PreviewOverlay.tsx:103

All three call setActiveLevelId directly (src/store/mapStore/editorSlice.ts:168 — a bare set, no building sync), and searchTargets spans every building's levels (PreviewOverlay.tsx:389-416). In a multi-building project, picking a search result in Building B renders B's floor while BuildingSelector still shows Building A and FloorSelector still lists A's floors — with a wrong "current floor" fallback (FloorSelector.tsx:35-37 falls back to canvasData.levels[0] / options.at(-1)).

Related: publicDefaultLevelId (src/lib/editor/levels.ts:132-136) is building-agnostic levels[0], which only lands in the default building when that building's levels happen to sit first in the array.

Fix direction

One guard where every path converges: have setActiveLevelId re-point selectedBuildingId to the target level's building (implicit default when the level carries no stamp). That fixes all three call sites at once instead of patching each.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Search pick, ?panoId deep link, and tour sync into another building update the building selector and floor list to that building
  • Selecting a level inside the current building does not change the selection
  • Legacy projects (no buildings) are unaffected
  • Unit test: cross-building setActiveLevelId re-points the selected building
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #565: Per-building scale never reaches indoor Z — height jumps at the outdoor threshold (PRD #536 R15)
issues.main_description_html:
PRD #536 validation gap 5 of 5 (R15).

Description

A building's mapTransform.scale scales its footprint in XY (via makeBuildingRecordTransform, src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:197-216) but never reaches Z indoors: wall and slab heights use only the project-wide canvasData.mapScale (geojson-utils.ts:538 zScale, levelBaseHeights at 379-388). That contradicts the file's own 1:1 invariant comment (lines 536-537).

Meanwhile outdoorGeoJson does multiply the shell height by the building's scale (geojson-utils.ts:781-785). Net effect: a scaled building gets wider but not taller indoors, and its height visibly jumps when the viewer crosses the indoor/outdoor zoom threshold.

Fix direction

Compose the building's mapTransform.scale into the indoor zScale / level base heights the same way outdoor massing already does, so a scaled building keeps 1:1 proportions and its height is continuous across the outdoor↔indoor transition.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Scaling a building scales its indoor wall/slab heights proportionally
  • Building height matches between outdoor massing and indoor rendering
  • Buildings with no mapTransform.scale, and legacy projects, are unchanged
  • Unit test: indoor Z follows the per-building scale, and matches the outdoor shell height
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer

issues.display_title: Issue #566: Second building's floors float above the first building's stack (PRD #536)
issues.main_description_html:
PRD #536 validation gap 6 of 6 — found while investigating the Z handling in #565, confirmed by test.

Description

levelBaseHeights (src/lib/map/geojson-utils.ts:378-390) accumulates one running height over every level in canvasData.levels, with no notion of buildings. In a multi-building project the second building's ground floor therefore inherits the first building's total stack height as its base altitude.

Verified: buildings A (2 floors × 3m) and B (1 floor), levels [a1, a2, b1] → b1 base = 6, expected 0.

Because levelBaseHeights is the single source of truth for floor altitude, every consumer floats with it: 3D walls and slabs (canvasDataToGeoJson, geojson-utils.ts:541), canvas labels and markers (useFloorPlanLabels.ts:119), map object markers (MapObjectMarkers.tsx:113), pano connection lines (panoConnections.ts:49), preview pin and direction dots (PreviewOverlay.tsx:129,277,323), selection layers (usePreviewSelectionLayers.ts:138), and tour sync (useTourSync.ts:77).

Meanwhile outdoorGeoJson stacks each building independently from base 0 (geojson-utils.ts:781-785), so a second building's massing sits on the ground while its indoor model hovers above it.

Fix direction

Reset the accumulator per building — group with the same rule as groupLevelsByBuilding (geojson-utils.ts:741-750; no buildingId = first building) so each building's floors stack from 0. Legacy projects (no buildings) keep one group and are unchanged.

Acceptance Criteria

  • Each building's floors stack from ground level, independent of other buildings
  • Legacy projects (no building records) produce identical heights to today
  • Indoor floor altitude matches the outdoor massing base for the same building
  • Unit test: second building's ground floor has base 0
  • pnpm test, pnpm lint, tsc --noEmit green

Assigned to: Ibnu Rizqia Ramadan — Developer
